claims.statement: useGame opens a single useStream on the `chess` assistant per game, using an SDK client built per session by sessionClient, and every submit carries configurable built by configurableOf from the game's record (the settings version first, then every setting key in order, nothing else; DEFAULT_CONTEXT only as a stand-in when there is no record), run_name chess-web with tag web, metadata surface web, and multitaskStrategy reject.

The web UI stores the current game's thread id in the `thread` URL query parameter via history.replaceState; when useStream reports a new thread id and the hook is still mounted, it binds the id and writes it to the URL, and the browser stores nothing per game because the game's setup lives in the thread.

On load, App seats the thread found in the URL with no chosen record so its setup comes from the thread; a new game or rematch clears the URL thread and creates a seat with a higher number and a chosen side, context and starting FEN (a rematch swaps sides and keeps context and start), remounting the keyed Table so useStream starts a fresh thread; a seat auto-starts when the opponent is to move in the starting position, and the Table sends that start once on mount guarded by a ref.

Human commands get message ids memoized per hook instance (one game) by the key ply:content, deliberately excluding the thread id because a new game's first command is sent before a thread exists, so a resend of the same command at the same position reuses the id, which the server treats as a no-op for already-consumed ids.

useGame's play sends the UCI move as a human message with an optimistic pendingMove shown until the submit settles, start sends `go`, and retry submits empty input to resume a pending turn because a fresh `go` is rejected while a turn is pending.

The Table locks the board when the game has no record or has not finished loading, when viewing an earlier ply, while loading, after the game ends, while a turn is pending, or while an optimistic move is in flight, and it swallows the SDK's 'a run is already in flight' rejection while surfacing other submit errors.

Auth failures (HTTP status 401/403, or SDK request messages anchored at the start as HTTP/Protocol/Thread state request failures with 401/403, so a model provider's 401 inside a run does not match) show a 'Sign-in needed' banner with an Open settings action; the Settings dialog has no editable setting and only describes the current session and offers Sign out for any session other than none.

Pressing Play in the New game dialog first checks the session with checkAccess, which POSTs to /assistants/search with the session's headers: 401/403 is 'missing' for a none session and 'rejected' (with the server's detail) otherwise, a network failure is 'unreachable', and anything else is ok; the game starts only on ok and only if the picks and starting position on screen are unchanged and still playable, and a late answer after unmount is ignored.

matchupOf derives the policy from the dialog picks (hybrid with both System 1 and an LLM, otherwise systemone or llm), rejects picking neither, an empty custom model spec, model_kwargs the server would hold back when an LLM plays, or an LLM game with memory on while the model's limit is being checked or could not be checked, turns memory off for a model without a known limit, and fills the unused model field with its default; a Random side is resolved once when Play is pressed.
With no game on screen the New game dialog cannot be closed, and opening Settings from it preserves the unsaved picks and typed starting position as a draft that is restored on return.

The server exposes GET /ui/config returning the graph id, JSON schema and defaults of ChessContext, but no frontend fetches it; the settings types, specs, labels, help and defaults are compiled in from chess-ui's generated settings, and the web app's CONTEXT_CHECKS is derived from the generated specs.

localStorage holds only the last New game setup, the reply-card view toggles and the display preferences for the game UI; stored setups are untrusted: they carry their settings version, a setup without a version loads as the defaults, knobs are migrated from their version with unknown keys dropped and each invalid value falls back to its own default, and an unreadable version trusts no stored knob.

apiUrl uses VITE_API_URL if set, otherwise http://localhost:2024 in dev, otherwise the page origin; by default the web build uses base /ui/ and outputs into the Python server package's static directory, which the server mounts at /ui when present.

packages/chess-ui is a private package whose exports point at TypeScript source (src/index.ts, styles.css, testing.ts) with no build step, so consuming apps compile it and must include its source in their Tailwind content globs and import its stylesheet.

chess-ui's ChessValues lists the only thread channels a UI may read (messages, start_fen, moves, plies, turns, outcome, error, and the optional draw_offers, setup and systemone_live); positions are rebuilt client-side by replaying moves, stopping silently at the first move chess.js rejects because the server is authoritative.

liveAnalysis returns the latest AI text after the current turn opened (or after the last human message), skipping AI messages already committed as a ply's message, so a previous move's analysis is never shown as live.

apps/review is built as a single dependency-free CommonJS bundle exporting render(data, container, metadata) for the LangSmith custom-app sandbox, with code splitting disabled and NODE_ENV defined as production outside Vitest; render creates the root, stylesheet and api dependencies once and re-renders in place so host updates do not reset loads.

The review app talks only to the LangSmith API through window.langsmith.call: it lists only the agent's tracing projects (langchain-chess-production, then langchain-chess-local, the first being the default), queries threads by project and time window in pages of 20, then fetches the threads' last root runs and their game_review, grade_status and game_review_part feedback (paged 100 at a time) in parallel and joins them into games.

reviewsByRun only considers feedback with a run_id and feedback_source metadata grader 'lcchess grade' (other feedback under the keys is ignored), takes the newest game_review header per run and its game_review_part parts; readReview treats a null value as invalid, joins a version-2 header with its generation's complete, contiguous parts into a version-1 shape, and parseReview classifies the result as graded only for a complete version-1 review with well-formed evals and ply grades and one eval per position, otherwise as invalid with the first problem found.

A review game's values are the last root run's outputs only when they validate as a game record (a UCI moves array plus well-shaped optional start_fen, plies, turns, outcome, draw_offers and systemone_live); otherwise the app shows 'No game record', and ungraded games show a 'Not graded yet' banner offering Analyze or an lcchess grade command.

GameView marks move-list entries with graded quality, draws the played move and the engine's differing best move as arrows, and from a graded review shows an eval bar from the per-position evals, engine header and lines, and an eval graph; for invalid reviews AnalysisBanner shows 'Review unreadable' offering Re-analyze or a forced lcchess grade regrade.
The review App tags each loaded games page with its project and since query so a stale response is never displayed for a newer query.

The pnpm workspace contains apps/web, apps/review, evals/reports and packages/*, with shared dependency versions pinned in a catalog (vite aliased to vite-plus-core) and referenced as catalog: so packages cannot drift.

Lint and format are configured only in the root vite.config.ts because Vite+ ignores nested lint/fmt blocks; lint is type-aware oxlint with rules-of-hooks and prefer-vite-plus-imports, and formatting ignores apps/server, libs, the Python parts of evals, openwiki and the generated chess-ui settings.

The web and review apps run jsdom Vitest over tests/**/*.test.{ts,tsx} with 100% line, function, branch and statement coverage thresholds; the review app writes coverage outside its directory because langsmith apps push ignores .gitignore.

Web tests replace useStream with a shared fake that records options, supports per-thread overrides and simulates thread-load outcomes, a separate suite exercises useGame on the real SDK over stubbed fetch, App takes a session plus injectable random, checkKey and modelFacts, and Root takes injectable config, signIn, check and storages, so tests are deterministic without a server or LangSmith.

The New game dialog asks the server about the chosen LLM via GET /ui/model (debounced 300 ms, sending the session's headers), which returns max_input_tokens and takes_effort; a number-or-null limit with a boolean takes_effort is known, and non-OK responses, malformed bodies and network errors are 'failed'; a null limit disables the Summarize memory option, a failed check blocks a game with memory on and offers Retry, and late answers for a no-longer-selected model are ignored.

The server's GameSetupMiddleware records the run's resolved ChessContext in a public, client-unwritable `setup` state channel only in the run that opened the game's first turn (both before and after the agent so failed or game-ending first turns still get it), never overwrites it, and never adds it to threads created before it existed.

The web UI continues a game from its thread: gameOf takes the context from the thread's `setup` only when loadRecorded accepts it (a valid version with exactly that version's keys, each valid, migrated to the current version), falls back to a new game's chosen context before its first turn is recorded, and otherwise yields no record so the game is view-only.

The human's side of a continued game is derived from the thread: the side of the last external ply, else the opposite of whoever played ply 0, else the picked side, else the side not to move in the start position.

useGame tracks each thread load by the SDK hydration promise as loading, missing (a clean load for a thread id that binds no thread), failed (rejected load) or ready, ignores superseded loads settling late, reloads with a new promise when a new session creates a new client, and the Table shows a Reload banner for failed loads and a not-on-server banner for missing threads while keeping the board locked.

The web app tolerates blocked localStorage: browserStorage returns null when storage access throws, writers report whether a save landed, and App shows a 'This browser isn't saving' banner when storage is blocked or a save fails.
The review app marks a graded review invalid when its ply UCIs do not match the game's moves, so evaluations are never drawn against a different move sequence.

The web build has two inputs, index.html (the play UI) and render.html (LangSmith's custom output renderer for the positions dataset, served at /ui/render.html), and gives Vite's preload helper its own chunk so render.html does not download the LangChain chunk.

The renderer's useParentMessage accepts a postMessage only when the page is embedded and the event source is the embedding window (trusting the parent window rather than an origin, since self-hosted LangSmith can be on any origin) and keeps the latest message readMessage can read.

readMessage ignores (returns null for) anything that is not an `output` or `reference` message; otherwise it builds the position from metadata.inputs (a valid start_fen and legally replaying moves plus legal moves) and returns a Stockfish reference (evals for every ranked move), a System 1 output (ranked moves with confidence and margin, or a failed ranking with its error), or `unreadable` with the first reason.

The renderer draws a locked chess-ui Board from the mover's side with the top three moves as arrows, next to a Stockfish eval table or System 1's top moves with confidence, margin, tournament, requests and latency, and follows the system colour scheme rather than the play UI's stored theme because LangSmith sends none.

The renderer URL is set on the positions dataset by `lcchess-evals positions upload --renderer-url`, which writes it into the dataset's iframe_config and requires an absolute https URL; render-preview.html is a dev-only page that is not a build input.

The New game dialog's Import reads a JSON file and loads it with chess-ui's loadSettings (version required and not newer than the app's, unknown keys and invalid values rejected, resolved over the defaults), replacing pickers and knobs while keeping the picked side, and shows the error as 'Couldn't import that setup' otherwise.
The New game dialog's Export downloads opponent.json containing configurableOf(context), the same object a run sends as configurable, and is enabled only while the matchup is playable.

chess-ui's generated/settings.ts (with settings.schema.json and opponent.schema.json) is written by `mise run generate:settings` from the Python ChessContext via langchain_chess_server.codegen, holding the settings version, types, specs, labels, help, defaults, per-version defaults and model_kwargs rules; it must not be hand-edited because a server test fails when committed files are stale.

chess-ui's settings.ts hand-mirrors the Python settings loading (version checks, migrations, loadSettings, loadRecorded, model_kwargs rules) and its tests run the shared cases in libs/systemone/tests/fixtures/settings-cases.json so the TypeScript and Python loaders agree.

The review app's Analyze writes a grade_status 'analyzing' feedback mark, creates a per-thread sandbox from the langchain-chess-grader snapshot with explicit delegated permissions, waits for it to be ready and launches a detached `lcchess grade ... --sandbox-job`; on launch failure it deletes the mark and sandbox and reports a readable reason, and the per-thread sandbox name makes a second start conflict rather than run twice.

The review app reads this grader's newest grade_status mark per run; an analyzing mark older than 10 minutes is treated as stalled, a failed mark carries the job's log, and retrying a failed or stalled job first deletes the old sandbox and mark.

The deployed web UI is hosted on GitHub Pages: the pages workflow builds apps/web with BASE_PATH set to the repository path, OUT_DIR dist, VITE_API_URL set to the agent deployment's URL and the VITE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, VITE_LANGSMITH_ORGANIZATION_ID and VITE_LANGSMITH_SSO_SLUG sign-in variables, is skipped until VITE_API_URL is set, and the server deployment ships without the static build while still answering /ui/config and /ui/model.

For an LLM that the server says takes no reasoning effort, the web app sends reasoning_effort null and disables the effort select, blocks Play while the effort check is pending if an effort would be sent, and blocks it when model_kwargs still set an effort for such a model; a failed model-facts request counts as taking an effort because the server checks again.

A new web game from a non-standard starting position opens with a single `position` input (never a message) carrying the start FEN and, for a human first move, that move; the hook resends exactly that packet on retry until the server accepts the root (any turn exists), and an error response with no turn marks the start as rejected, which the Table answers with a Change position action that reopens the dialog with that FEN.

The New game dialog's Starting position field accepts a FEN (empty for the standard position), validates it with chess-ui's validateStart, normalizes and previews it, blocks Play while invalid, and the starting position is never stored with the saved setup.

The web Table offers Resign (with a confirmation) and Offer draw, which useGame sends as human messages `resign <side>` and `draw <side>` carrying the human's side because the server does not know which side is human; these control commands are never resent automatically.

The web Table exports the game as FEN or PGN (copied, downloaded as langchain-chess-<thread>.pgn, or opened on Lichess), with pgnOf naming the players 'You' and the opponent label and commenting the opponent, changed knobs and thread id, and falls back to a dialog showing the text when clipboard access is refused.

main.tsx mounts Root, which renders a misconfiguration banner when VITE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID is set without VITE_LANGSMITH_ORGANIZATION_ID, and otherwise renders by session status: an empty busy page while checking, the SignIn screen when signed out, and App with the session and an onSignOut callback when signed in.

A web Session is none, apiKey or oauth; sessionHeaders maps it to no headers, x-api-key, or an Authorization Bearer token fetched per request, and sessionClient builds an SDK Client with apiKey null that adds those headers to every request and stream via onRequest.

useSession resumes a tab's sign-in in order: a LangSmith OAuth sign-in, then this tab's stored API key, then a none session if the server accepts an unauthenticated access check; an unreachable server or a failed resume leaves the user signed out with a problem, and signing out clears the tab's API key.

The web UI keeps an API key only in sessionStorage under langchain-chess:api-key, keeps only the last LangSmith account's email in localStorage, and deletes the legacy localStorage key langchain-chess:app where older versions kept the API key.
